name: Pachmarhi
description: Pachmarhi is the only hill station in Madhya Pradesh, sitting at roughly 1,067 metres in the Satpura range. It suits travellers who want a mix of forest walks, sandstone cave temples, and modest waterfalls without the crowds of more famous hill stations. The pace is slow, facilities are basic-to-mid-range, and the real draw is the dense sal and teak forest rather than luxury or nightlife.

attractions.name: Bee Falls (Jamuna Prapat)
attractions.description: A 35-metre cascade that drops into a clear pool, reachable by a paved trail of about 1.5 km from the parking area. It is one of the most visited spots in Pachmarhi and can get crowded on weekends and public holidays.

attractions.name: Dhoopgarh
attractions.description: The highest point in the Satpura range at 1,352 metres, offering panoramic sunrise and sunset views over layered forested ridges. The road goes most of the way up, with a short walk to the summit, but it requires a forest department jeep permit and can be cold and windy.

attractions.name: Pandava Caves
attractions.description: A group of five rock-cut Buddhist caves dating to around the 1st century CE, later associated in local legend with the Pandavas. The caves are small and unadorned but the surrounding forest and sandstone outcrops make the setting pleasant.

attractions.name: Chauragarh Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple perched at 1,326 metres, reached by climbing roughly 1,300 uneven stone steps from the jeep road terminus. The trek is steep and takes 1.5 to 2 hours each way; pilgrims carry tridents (trishuls) up as offerings, creating a striking visual. Not suitable for people with knee or heart conditions.

attractions.name: Jatashankar Cave Temple
attractions.description: A natural cave sheltering a Shiva lingam, reached by descending into a narrow gorge with rock formations that resemble matted hair (jata). The descent involves slippery steps and low headroom in places; the cave itself stays cool even in summer.

attractions.name: Handi Khoh
attractions.description: A sheer 300-foot gorge blanketed in dense forest, viewable from a fenced lookout. There is no way down into the gorge, so the visit is purely a viewpoint experience; the scale is impressive but the stop is brief.

attractions.name: Duchess Falls
attractions.description: One of the tallest waterfalls in Madhya Pradesh at around 100 metres, set deep inside the forest and requiring a 3 km walk each way on a forest trail. Unlike the busier Bee Falls, this one sees far fewer visitors and retains a genuinely wild feel, but the trail can be slippery after rain.

attractions.name: Satpura National Park Jeep Safari
attractions.description: Satpura is one of the less-crowded tiger reserves in India, with rugged Denwa river terrain and a realistic chance of spotting leopard, sloth bear, gaur, and wild dog even when tigers are elusive. Booking through the forest department is mandatory and zones are limited, so advance reservation is essential.

attractions.name: Priyadarshini Point (Forsyth Point)
attractions.description: A sunset viewpoint with a wide valley panorama, named after Indira Gandhi and formerly known as Forsyth Point after the British officer who discovered Pachmarhi. The view is sweeping but the site itself is bare and commercialised with snack stalls; worth combining with other nearby viewpoints rather than visiting alone.

attractions.name: Rajat Prapat (Silver Falls)
attractions.description: A slender 107-metre waterfall that appears as a silver thread against dark basalt cliffs; it is best seen from a viewpoint rather than up close, and flow is strongest July through September. This is a genuine hidden-gem stop because most jeep tours skip it in favour of Bee Falls, yet the visual impact at full monsoon flow is striking.
